main_statements.label: Theorem 1
main_statements.quantifiers: forall integer m>=1, forall complex u in H^m
limits: Both source clauses hold for every integer m>=1 and every original complex H^m input. The scalar Hamiltonian K_m has its full native complex H^(m-1) domain, including the L2 mass endpoint. No finite-gap, smoothness, real-type or nonzero-mean hypothesis enters theorem1.

The scalar spectral Hamiltonians are extracted on every smooth complex periodic profile from literal samples of the independent physical Hill discriminant. A fixed local inverse of sinh recovers a small phase at r_j=pi*(j+1/2), and recursive scaled limits extract its coefficients. All those limits are proved to exist. The normalization is K_(s+1)=(-i/2) times the coefficient of (2*r)^(-(2*s+1)).

The extensions from all smooth complex profiles to the full native complex Sobolev domains are constructed and proved uniquely continuous there, using smooth density. The independent scalar Riccati hierarchy realizes them and proves they are entire analytic. No candidate extension, analyticity, gradient, spectral identification, or diagonal finite-gap density is an input assumption.

The scalar gradient comes from the actual Frechet derivative of the uniquely extended spectral Hamiltonian, through the certified native Sobolev bilinear duality. Its Gardner field is the actual period-one tempered distribution derivative. The field identity is proved as equality of those genuine distributions.

The source finite-gap physical Hill primitive has the convergent Laurent series with exactly these native spectral coefficients, retaining its factor 2, original intrinsic gap labels, zero mean and collapsed exterior gaps. General smooth complex coefficient extraction does not assert convergence of the infinite Laurent series outside the finite-gap setting.
